easy.def: To do what you are told.
easy.example: My dog will obey when I say "sit."

more.def: To do what a person, rule, or law tells you to do.
more.example: Drivers must obey the traffic signs.

easy.def: A thing you can see and touch.
easy.example: A ball is a round object.

more.def: A thing that you can see and touch, but that is not alive.
more.example: There was a shiny object at the bottom of the pond.

easy.example: We observe the ants as they work.

more.def: To watch someone or something closely in order to learn about it.
more.example: The class observed how the caterpillar changed over two weeks.

easy.def: A very big sea of salt water.

more.def: One of the huge bodies of salt water that cover most of the Earth.
more.example: The Pacific Ocean is the largest ocean in the world.

easy.def: Something that is as different as it can be.
easy.example: Hot is the opposite of cold.

more.def: A person or thing that is completely different from another.

easy.def: To go around and around something in space.

more.def: To travel in a curved path around a planet, moon, or star.
more.example: The moon orbits the Earth about once every month.

easy.def: A place where fruit trees grow.
easy.example: We picked apples in the orchard.

more.def: A piece of land where fruit or nut trees are grown.
more.example: The orchard was full of ripe peaches.

easy.example: It was an ordinary day at school.

more.def: Usual or normal; not different or special in any way.
more.example: It looked like an ordinary rock, but there was a crystal inside.

easy.example: Let's organize the toys by color.

more.def: To arrange things in a neat order, or to plan an event.
more.example: We organized the books by author on the shelf.
On sunny days, our class eats lunch outdoors.

easy.def: A part of air that we need to breathe.

more.def: A gas in the air that people, animals, and plants need to live.
more.example: Fish use their gills to take oxygen from the water.
